h: Making the Most of a Big London Day Out
p: County Hall has quite a back story. The grand riverside building was once the headquarters of London's local government, and these days it's home to a whole cluster of attractions, with the aquarium tucked into the lower floors. It first opened as the London Aquarium in 1997 and has been one of the South Bank's big crowd-pullers ever since.

Because it's slap bang in the middle of tourist London, timing is everything. School holidays, weekends and rainy afternoons are when it's heaving, so if you can, get in early in the day and you'll have a much calmer wander past the tanks. Booking ahead online is the way to go, as you'll pick a time slot and avoid the walk-up queue.

A few tips for families. Pace the visit with snack breaks outside rather than trying to do everything in one long push, especially with toddlers. Let the older kids take charge of the map and spot the creatures on the information boards, and have a quick toilet stop before you start, as once you're on the route it's a one-way journey.

Afterwards, the area around you is a goldmine. Jubilee Gardens, right next to the London Eye, is a handy patch of green for the kids to let off steam. River boats leave from the London Eye Pier if you fancy seeing the city from the water, heading down past St Paul's and towards Tower Bridge. Cross Westminster Bridge and you're at Parliament Square and Westminster Abbey, while a stroll east along the river brings you to the Southbank Centre's riverside terraces and weekend food stalls. It's very easy to turn a couple of hours with the sharks into a full day.
